arxiv-1504-01960.title: 2-Selmer parity for hyperelliptic curves in quadratic extensions
arxiv-1504-01960.creator: Adam Morgan
arxiv-1504-01960.description: Abstract . We study the 2-parity conjecture for Jacobians of hyperelliptic curves over number fields. Under some mild assumptions on their reduction, we prove the conjecture over quadratic extensions of the base field. The proof proceeds via a generalisation of a formula of Kramer and Tunnell relating local invariants of the curve, which may be of independent interest.

arxiv-2104-07462.title: Bi-fidelity Reduced Polynomial Chaos Expansion for Uncertainty Quantification Journal: Computational Mechanics
arxiv-2104-07462.creator: Felix Newberry, Jerrad Hampton, Kenneth Jansen, Alireza Doostan
arxiv-2104-07462.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Felix Newberry, Jerrad Hampton, Kenneth Jansen, Alireza Doostan. A ubiquitous challenge in design space explora-tion or uncertainty quantification of complex engineering problems is the minimization of computational cost. A useful tool to ease the burden of solving such systems is model reduction. This work considers a stochastic model reduction method (SMR), in the context of polynomial chaos (PC) expansions, where low-fidelity (LF) samples are leveraged to form a stochastic reduced basis.

arxiv-2106-11100.title: Alternative rings whose associators are not zero-divisors
arxiv-2106-11100.creator: Erwin Kleinfeld Yoav Segev
arxiv-2106-11100.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Erwin Kleinfeld Yoav Segev. The purpose of this short note is to prove that if R R is an alternative ring whose associators are not zero-divisors, then R R has no zero divisors. By a result of Bruck and Kleinfeld, if, in addition, the characteristic of R R is not 2 , 2, then the central quotient of R R is an octonion division algebra over some field. 2000 Mathematics Subject Classification Primary: 17D05 ; Secondary: 17A35 1.

arxiv-2207-10772.title: Deep Sufficient Representation Learning via Mutual Information
arxiv-2207-10772.creator: Siming Zhengabel=e1, mark]simingzheng@cuhk.edu.hk, Yuanyuan Linabel=e2, mark]ylin@sta.cuhk.edu.hk, Jian Huangabel=e3, mark]j.huang@polyu.edu.hk
arxiv-2207-10772.description: Abstract We propose a mutual information-based sufficient representation learning (MSRL) approach, which uses the variational formulation of mutual information and leverages the approximation power of deep neural networks. MSRL learns a sufficient representation with the maximum mutual information with the response and a user-selected distribution. It can easily handle multi-dimensional continuous or categorical response variables.

arxiv-2309-12221.title: Optimizing the Wasserstein GAN for TeV Gamma Ray Detection with VERITAS
arxiv-2309-12221.creator: Kameswara Mantha
arxiv-2309-12221.description: Abstract The observation of very-high-energy (VHE, E>100 GeV) gamma rays is mediated by the imaging atmospheric Cherenkov technique (IACTs). At these energies, gamma rays interact with the atmosphere to create a cascade of electromagnetic air showers that are visible to the IACT cameras on the ground with distinct morphological and temporal features.

arxiv-2403-10507.title: Demystifying Faulty Code with LLM: Step-by-Step Reasoning for Explainable Fault Localization
arxiv-2403-10507.creator: Ratnadira Widyasari, Jia Wei Ang, Truong Giang Nguyen, Neil Sharma, David Lo
arxiv-2403-10507.description: Abstract Fault localization is a critical process that involves identifying specific program elements responsible for program failures. Manually pinpointing these elements, such as classes, methods, or statements, which are associated with a fault is laborious and time-consuming. To overcome this challenge, various fault localization tools have been developed. These tools typically generate a ranked list of suspicious program elements.

arxiv-2407-00832.title: Boxer: FaaSt Ephemeral Elasticity for Off-the-Shelf Cloud Applications 137
arxiv-2407-00832.creator: Michael Wawrzoniak 1 , Rodrigo Bruno 2 , Ana Klimovic 1 , Gustavo Alonso 1 1 Systems Group, Dept. of Computer Science, ETH Zurich 2 INESC-ID/Técnico, U. Lisboa
arxiv-2407-00832.description: Abstract Abstract Elasticity is a key property of cloud computing. However, elasticity is offered today at the granularity of virtual machines, which take tens of seconds to start. This is insufficient to react to load spikes and sudden failures in latency sensitive applications, leading users to resort to expensive overprovisioning.

arxiv-2508-00544.title: PaPaformer: Language Model from Pre-trained Parallel Paths
arxiv-2508-00544.creator: Joonas Tapaninaho, Mourad Oussalah
arxiv-2508-00544.description: Abstract . The training of modern large-language models requires an increasingly amount of computation power and time. Even smaller variants, such as small-language models (SLMs), take several days to train in the best-case scenarios, often requiring multiple GPUs. This paper explores methods to train and evaluate decoder-only transformer-based language models in hours instead of days/weeks.

arxiv-2508-14930.title: Hybrelighter: Combining Deep Anisotropic Diffusion and Scene Reconstruction for On-device Real-time Relighting in Mixed Reality
arxiv-2508-14930.creator: Hanwen Zhao, John Akers, Baback Elmieh, Ira Kemelmacher-Shlizerman
arxiv-2508-14930.description: Abstract Mixed Reality scene relighting, where virtual changes to lighting conditions realistically interact with physical objects, producing authentic illumination and shadows, can be used in a variety of applications. One such application in real estate could be visualizing a room at different times of day and placing virtual light fixtures.

pmc-10493093.creator: Xianhong Yang, Yunlin Ren, Huachu Liu, Yan Ten, Yang Ding, Shasha Fan, Xiaohua Tao, Wei Lu
pmc-10493093.description: We report a case of 32-year-old patient who presented with painless erythematous plaque gradually ulcerated for 9 years. He had a history of pulmonary tuberculosis 12 years ago and was cured by the treatment of 2HRZE/4HR. The laboratory examination of t-spot and PPD skin test was positive.

pmc-10648019.title: High-Energy Radiation Effects on Silicon NPN Bipolar Transistor Electrical Performance: A Study with 1 MeV Proton Irradiation
pmc-10648019.creator: Haddou EL Ghazi, Redouane En-nadir, Anouar Jorio, Mohamed A. Basyooni-M. Kabatas
pmc-10648019.description: This study investigates the degradation of the silicon NPN transistor’s emitter-base junction, specifically the 2N2219A model, under both forward and reverse polarization. We examine the current–voltage characteristics under the influence of 1 MeV proton irradiation at various fluencies, which are 5.3×108,5.3×1010,5×1011,5×1012, and 5×1013 protons/cm², all conducted at 307 K.

pmc-11521551.title: Capacity-Building Through Digital Approaches: Evaluating the Feasibility and Effectiveness of eLearning to Introduce Subcutaneous DMPA Self-Injection in Senegal and Uganda
pmc-11521551.creator: Siri Wood, Ericka Roberts, Aurora Anna Stout, Alain Kaboré, Allen Namagembe, Jane Cover, Marème Dia Ndiaye, Mouminatou Diokh, Farmata Sèye, Beth Balderston
pmc-11521551.description: This evaluation of online training for health workers to counsel clients wishing to self-inject subcutaneous DMPA suggests that online training can be effective while saving time and money. Further, eLearning courses work best when complemented with supportive supervision to help health workers correctly apply their knowledge through hands-on practice.

pmc-11522143.title: The impact of task measurements on sequential dependence: a comparison between temporal reproduction and discrimination tasks
pmc-11522143.creator: Si Cheng, Siyi Chen, Xuefeng Yang, Zhuanghua Shi
pmc-11522143.description: Decisions about a current stimulus are influenced by previously encountered stimuli, leading to sequential bias. However, the specific processing levels at which serial dependence emerges remain unclear. Despite considerable evidence pointing to contributions from perceptual and post-perceptual processes, as well as response carryover effects impacting subsequent judgments, research into how different task measurements affect sequential dependencies is limited.

pmc-11713079.title: A novel culprit in glucose hypometabolism in Alzheimer’s disease
pmc-11713079.creator: Ylauna Penalva, Marina Ruelas Hernandez, Jessica Cinkornpumin, Mari Kaartinen, William Pastor, Lisa Munter
pmc-11713079.description: BackgroundAlzheimer’s disease is characterized by early decreases in cerebral glucose metabolism which are linked to reduced glucose transporter 1 (GLUT1) expression at the blood‐brain barrier (BBB). Another key disease hallmark is the abundance of Aβ peptides as plaques in the brain which arise from the processing of the amyloid precursor protein (APP).

pmc-12420116.title: Sexual Harassment Among Medical residents and interns in Sfax: Psychological Impact
pmc-12420116.creator: S. Ajmi, F. Cherif, O. Bouattour, D. Mnif, I. Feki, R. Masmoudi, J. Masmoudi
pmc-12420116.description: IntroductionSexual harassment (SH) is a pervasive issue, particularly in workplace environments. The medical field, especially in hospitals, is not immune to this issue with medical residents and interns often being disproportionately affected. SH can have profound psychological, emotional, and physical consequences, which can impair professional performance and well-being.

pmc-12555173.title: Analysis of primary healthcare center closures following the Finnish structural reform
pmc-12555173.creator: V Väisänen, T Sinervo
pmc-12555173.description: BackgroundWhile accessible primary healthcare is a cornerstone of well-functioning health systems, various factors, such as health system reforms, may affect the provision of services. The recent Finnish structural reform is a good example, as the new counties, driven by budgetary deficits, are currently adjusting their service networks, leading to public health center closures.

Rose distillation wastewater (RDW), the major by-product of rose processing, still contains a significant load of polyphenolic compounds.

pmc-12608804.creator: Mengmeng Yang, Lay Sheng Ewe, Weng Kean Yew, Sanxing Deng, Sieh Kiong Tiong, George Yannis, Anastasios Doulamis

pmc-12780212.title: National human footprint maps for Peru and Ecuador
pmc-12780212.creator: Jose Aragon-Osejo, Lenin Beltrán, Juan Iglesias, Hólger Zambrano, Daniel Borja, Carlos Oñate, Francisco Simbaña, Freddy Valencia, Karen Rodríguez De la Vera, Luis Poveda, Fernando Proaño, Lorena Parra, María Chacón, William Llactayo, Tatiana Pequeño Saco, Walter Huamani, German Marchand, Raúl Tinoco
pmc-12780212.description: Human Footprint (HF) maps score human pressures based on their influence and integrate them into a single spatial index to assess the naturalness of ecosystems. We produced a historical series of national HF maps for Peru and Ecuador for Sustainable Development Goal 15 (SDG15) reporting.

pmc-13225026.title: Willingness of CDC Staff to Participate in Continuing Education in China: A Bayesian Network Analysis
pmc-13225026.creator: Jialin Lu, Nan Meng, Yanping Wang, Kexin Wang, Peng Wang, Yiran Gao, Min Wei, Huan Liu, Qunhong Wu
pmc-13225026.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectiveTo investigate the willingness of China Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (C-CDC) staff in Northeast China to participate in continuing education and identify the factors associated with such willingness.MethodsThis study adopted a cross-sectional design using stratified cluster sampling. Based on Expectancy-Value-Cost (EVC) and Job Demands-Resources (JD-R) theories, literature evidence, and study objectives, the survey variable system was constructed to cover multiple dimensions.

pmc-13661237.title: Integrated memristor for mitigating reverse-bias in perovskite solar cells
pmc-13661237.creator: Mahdi Mohammadi, Fuxiang Ji, Tristan Sachsenweger, Kazem Meraji, Sharun Parayil Shaji, Wolfgang Tress
pmc-13661237.description: Perovskite solar cells (PSCs) with power-conversion efficiencies comparable to established technologies hold huge promise for becoming the future photovoltaic technology, also given their versatility, low-cost and energy-efficient fabrication processes1. However, PSCs are not stable under moderate reverse bias2–4, an unavoidable situation under real-world operation, for instance, caused by partial shading of a module or installation with PSCs connected in series.

pmc-13685198.title: Knowledge, attitude, practice and symptoms of computer vision syndrome: a comparative study among university students and support staff
pmc-13685198.creator: Tadpong Tantipanjaporn, Soranun Surapad, Kwanjira Yatong, Kiattisak Satamunai, Pattraporn Chomchey, Sudawadee Yasaka, Pantip Hinhumpatch, Kanpitcha Kiatkitroj, Sutthisaranyupong Chanyo
pmc-13685198.description: BackgroundDespite the high prevalence of computer vision syndrome (CVS) in academic settings, there is a lack of comparative data regarding how different university cohorts manage these risks. This study evaluated and compared CVS knowledge, attitudes, preventive practices, and symptoms between undergraduate students and supporting staff at a university in Thailand.MethodsThe study included 485 participants (269 students, 216 staff).

uslaw-usc-t28-s1396.title: 28 U.S.C. § 1396 — Internal revenue taxes
uslaw-usc-t28-s1396.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t28-s1396.description: United States Code, Title 28 (Judiciary And Judicial Procedure); Part IV (Jurisdiction And Venue); Chapter 87 (District Courts; Venue). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. Any civil action for the collection of internal revenue taxes may be brought in the district where the liability for such tax accrues, in the district of the taxpayer’s residence, or in the district where the return was.
